chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about Itikaf (seclusion in a mosque). He said: Itikaf is not valid except in the Sacred Mosque, or the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), or the Mosque of Kufa, or a general congregation mosque, and you should fast as long as you are in Itikaf.

key_terms.الِاعْتِكَافِ: Itikaf, spiritual seclusion in a mosque
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الرَّسُولِ: The Mosque of the Messenger (Prophet Muhammad SAWW)

ai.seo_question: Where is Itikaf valid and is fasting required?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies that valid Itikaf is restricted to the three holiest sites in Shia tradition—the Masjid al-Haram, Masjid al-Nabi, and Masjid al-Kufa—alongside congregational mosques, reflecting the emphasis on communal worship. It further mandates fasting as a prerequisite for the seclusion, linking physical discipline with spiritual devotion. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential distinction between general mosque usage and the specific sanctity required for this act of worship.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘Heasws was asked about the Itikaaf.

Heasws said: ‘The Itikaaf is not correct except in the Sacred Masjid, or Masjid of the Rasoolsaww, or Masjid of Al-Kufa, or a general Masjid, and you should be Fasting for as long as you are in Itikaaf’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about ’Ttikaf.

He (the Imam) said, ‘Without Masjid ’Ttikaf is not valid, only in Masjid like Masjid al-Haram, Masjid of the Messenger of Allah, Masjid al-Kufah or Masjid al-Jami‘ and you must fast in the time you are in the state of ’Ttikaf.’”
